# A patrolling shopkeeper's walk lasts one step (851-3527, docs/quirks.md §1), and the wiki clip
# quirks/shopkeeper-patrol-one-step. A staged scene (written by wiki-clips --replays from a scene spec,
# docs/wiki-media.md): it boots, loads this custom level from the title's load-level menu (240), and plays the
# scene's inputs from 241, its frame 0. The player (@) stands still at the left of a flat room, and the level
# editor's ! is a shopkeeper on patrol (scrCreateTileObj sets status 4, PATROL) 14 blocks right of him:
#   1111111111111111111111111111111111111
#   1000000000000000000000000000000000001
#   ...  (5 rows like it)
#   10@0000000000000!00000000000000000001
#   1111111111111111111111111111111111111
#   1111111111111111111111111111111111111
# PATROL counts down rand(20,50) steps and turns to WALK (status 1) facing a random way. WALK's turn back to
# PATROL tests collision_point(x-1, y) (facing left) or (x+16, y) (right), a wall beside his head, without the
# y+16 floor test the same lines have in oAlien's and oManTrap's walks (their turn at a ledge), so in open
# ground it patrols again on the next step, after setting xVel to 1.5 anyway. He coasts to a stop over ten
# steps (friction, 0.1 a step) and waits again: ten one-step walks
# (240, 270, 298, 330, 369, 405, 444, 475, 506, 530), each PATROL again on the next frame. He never comes
# within reach of the player, who isn't hurt. Ends at 540.
# story: oShopkeeper.status=1@270..270 oShopkeeper.status=4@271..271 oShopkeeper.xVel=1.4@271..271
